items.title: About Co-Desk: Built By Founders for Coworking & Coliving Operators
items.snippet:
> Co-Desk (sometimes written as Codesk or CoDesk) is all-in-one SaaS software for managing coworking spaces and coliving houses. It handles bookings, billing (via Stripe Connect), access control, member and resident management, and community tools, all in a single platform. Founded in 2024, Co-Desk is built by operators for operators, with setup in under 30 minutes. Pricing is pay-as-you-go: EUR 0/month with 2.5% per Stripe transaction, or a Custom plan for non-Stripe setups. Website: https://co-desk.eu
[...]

- Pricing: EUR 0/month with 2.5% per Stripe transaction, or Custom for non-Stripe setups
- Contact: Get a demo or reach the sales team

# The Redacted Loop Series
[...]
Written by Founder [REDACTED]
[...]
The [REDACTED] Loop is the unvarnished, real-time diary of a solo founder building a geospatial FinTech network in the heart of St. Louis. Designed to rip local commerce away from the 30% margins of giant delivery apps, the "Loop" is a masterclass in localized economic warfare.

### The Redacted Loop: A Founders Diary pt.1: A Founder's Diary of Adrenaline, Code, and the 314's Moat
[...]
Forget the Silicon Valley playbook. You don't need a massive venture capital war chest or a team of MIT engineers to build a multi-billion-dollar infrastructure. You need a Replit console, an AI agent, and a geographic moat. The [REDACTED] Loop is the unvarnished, real-time diary of a solo founder building a geospatial FinTech network in the heart of St. Louis. Designed to rip local commerce away from the 30% margins of giant delivery apps, the "Loop" is a masterclass in localized economic warfare. This isn't a sanitized business memoir. This is a gritty, tactical survival guide for the modern builder. You will be in the room as the founder navigates catastrophic, AI-generated security flaws hours before launch, battles the ruthless monopolies of the Apple App Store, and executes the psychological hustle required to sign the first ten "Genesis Merchants" on the sticky floors of neighborhood dive bars. Whether you are a developer, a local business owner, or a startup founder staring at a blank terminal in the middle of the night, this audiobook provides the exact blueprint for surviving the "Traction Gap." In this audiobook, you will learn: The architecture of the "Pulse Radius" and how to use geofencing to physically move customers across a street. Why 10 loyal merchants in a single neighborhood is a more powerful moat than 500 scattered vanity sign-ups. How to leverage an AI Agent as your CTO—and how to fix the fatal "Trust-on-Client" security flaws it leaves behind. The "Clipboard Hustle" framework for selling disruptive tech to exhausted brick-and-mortar business owners. How to navigate the strict App Store mandates and build compliance armor for a real-money application. The code is written. The vault is locked. The engine is breathing. Welcome to the Loop.

items.snippet:
Emily Stewart - Founder, President at coexperiences | The Org
[...]
# Emily Stewart
[...]
### Founder, President
[...]
Emily Stewart is an accomplished professional with extensive experience in technology, project management, and community engagement. As the Founder and President of CoExperiences since March 2020, Emily leads initiatives focused on connection and belonging. Previously, Emily served as Forensic Technology Staff at EY, where responsibilities included designing databases, analyzing vast data sets, and creating dashboards for client presentations. Emily's background also includes UX/UI development at NetApp, project management and web development at NC State University, along with early career experience in customer service and community organization. Emily holds a Bachelor of Science in Information Technology and Business Administration from North Carolina State University.

items.title: limor fried | Founder Engineer
items.snippet:
# Limor Fried
[...]
Founder & Engineer at Adafruit
[...]
Founder Engineer at Adafruit Industries
[...]
I started Adafruit 2005 after I graduated from MIT. My goal was to create the best place online for learning electronics and making the best designed products for makers of all ages and skill levels. Adafruit has grown to over 100+ employees in the heart of NYC with a 50,000+ sq ft. factory. Adafruit has expanded offerings to include tools, equipment and electronics that I personally select, test and approve before going in to the Adafruit store. I was the first female engineer on the cover of WIRED magazine, awarded Entrepreneur magazine's Entrepreneur of the year, and was on the cover of Make: Vol. 57. I was a founding member of the NYC Industrial Business Advisory Council. Adafruit is ranked #11 in the top 20 USA manufacturing companies and #1 in New York City by Inc. 5000 "fastest growing private companies". Adafruit is featured in Google's Economic Impact Report. I was named a WHITEHOUSE CHAMPION OF CHANGE in 2016. Adafruit is a 100% woman owned company.
[...]
### Founder Engineer at Adafruit Industries (Current)
[...]
Department: General Management • Level: Founder
[...]
Adafruit Industries is a Appliances, Electrical, and Electronics Manufacturing company. Adafruit Industries is a company that specializes in DIY electronics and kits. They offer a wide range of tools, gadgets, and accessories for various industries such as robotics, CNC, and more. Adafruit Industries employs 42 people (+1.3% YoY, +1 person) and has an annual revenue of $43.1M, founded in 2005. Headquartered in New York City, New York, United States, operates in 5 countries (including Germany, Vietnam, United Kingdom, and Canada).
[...]
While studying engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Limor “Ladyada” Fried decided to create a company focused on supporting learning electronics for makers of all ages and skill levels. In 2005 she founded Adafruit which has grown to now employ more than 100 individuals in their 50,000 sq ft. NYC factory. Limor is committed to building both innovation and community and is known for creating resources for learning. She was the first female engineer on the cover of WIRED magazine and was awarded Entrepreneur magazine’s Entrepreneur of the Year in 2012 and was also on the NYC Industrial Business Advisory Council. Adafruit is a 100% woman-owned company. These individuals were selected by the White House for their personal passion and tireless efforts to make advances in technology and platforms, educational opportunities, or spaces that empower even more Americans to become tinkerers, inventors, and entrepreneurs. This celebration comes on the anniversary of the first-ever White House Maker Faire in June 2014 where President Obama launched the Nation of Makers initiative, an all-hands-on-deck call to make sure more students, entrepreneurs, and Americans of all backgrounds have access to a new class of technologies—such as 3D printers, laser cutters, and desktop machine tools—that are enabling more Americans to design, build, and manufacture just about anything. Last year, the President expanded the work and asked “all Americans to help unlock the potential of our Nation and ensure these opportunities reach all our young people, regardless of who they are or where they come from.” The Champions of Change program was created as an opportunity for the White House to feature individuals doing extraordinary things to empower and inspire members of their communities. The event will feature remarks by U.S. Chief Technology Officer Megan Smith and Thomas Kalil, Deputy Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. Show less
[...]
OpenSystems Media’s publication Embedded Computing Design called for nominations for the top innovators and most influential women of 2014. They received many inspirational, qualified nominations and chose several men and women from the list. Limor “Ladyada” Fried is an MIT engineer, open source hardware and software pioneer, and entrepreneur. She is the founder of the educational electronics company Adafruit. Her goal was to create the best place online for learning electronics and making the best-designed products for makers of all ages and skill levels. Fried was the first female engineer on the cover of WIRED magazine, an EFF Pioneer Award recipient, and was recently awarded Entrepreneur magazine’s Entrepreneur of the Year. Show less
[...]
Limor Fried of Adafruit: MIT electrical engineer Limor “Ladyada” Fried founded Adafruit Industries to bring the world of electronics to anyone willing to learn. Ever think you’d be able to be a robotics hobbyist? Or build circuits into your clothing and light your suspenders up with LEDs? The company sells do-it-yourself open-source electronics kits and educational materials for makers of all ages and skill levels. Adafruit has never needed to take loans or investments of any kind, Fried tells Newsweek. In 2013 Adafruit took in over $22 million in revenue. The company has more than 50 employees, and by the end of this year it plans to have more than 100. Since it was founded in 2005, Adafruit has filled 480,000 orders and sold over a million products in “just about every country in the world.” Show less
[...]
The magazine’s Entrepreneur of 2012, Limor Fried, founded Adafruit Industries in 2005 and through it, is educating and inspiring the next generation of engineers and scientists. The open-source hardware and electronics company not only designs a catalog full of cool tech products that clients can order–it gives away the step-by-step instructions and tutorials for them to learn how to do so themselves. Fried’s new badging system also makes learning exciting for kids, by rewarding them for mastering new tech-savvy skills, and furthers the educational mission of Adafruit Industries. Show less
[...]
Limor Fried was the sort of third-grader who took apart VCRs for fun. Gradually, she discovered that a hobby could become a degree–a bachelor’s and then a master’s in electrical engineering and computer science at MIT. Finally, she discovered it could become a business. During her student years, Fried would post photographs and detailed instructions of her latest experiments in hardware hacking. First, she built an audience, and then a company, Adafruit Industries. Through Adafruit, Fried (hacker handle: ladyada, after Ada Lovelace, the 19th century proto-programmer) sells DIY kits out of New York. Her best seller, something she calls the “Minty Boost,” is a backup battery pack for your iPod (or any USB device), nestled into a cute little Altoids can. It’s a good starter kit for someone making their first foray into hardware hacking–only a minimum amount of soldering necessary. Another of ladyada’s fruits is a cell phone jammer. In 2004, while still an MIT student, Fried tried to get work done in cafes–but couldn’t hear herself think, so ubiquitous were the cell phone conversations around her. So she brainstormed, and put together a device that disabled all cell phone signals around her. (When a Samsung rep later met Fried, he quipped: “Could you make one that just disables Nokia phones?”) As it turns out, the manufacture, sale, or even use of such a device is illegal in the U.S.–but writing about it is fine, and if someone theoretically wanted to learn how one could theoretically make such a thing, that information is also up on Fried’s site. Her company and site have made Fried something of a DIY goddess; she’s on the advisory board for Make Magazine, often speaking at its Maker Faire events. Fried’s approach is sometimes called “open-source hardware”–similar to open-source software, but instead of the source code being open and malleable, the source materials are. "What we’re trying to do is make electrical engineering exciting, cool, and fun.” Show less

# Emily Assender
[...]
### COO & Co-founder
[...]
Emily Assender is a seasoned executive with extensive experience in strategic partnerships and business development across various industries. Currently serving as COO and Co-founder at Revelesco since March 2024, Emily leads efforts to provide critical coaching and strategic support for startups and scaleups. Previously, Emily held roles such as Director at Okra Partners Ltd., focusing on building partnerships for B2B SaaS businesses, and Vice President of Strategic Partnerships at Gatekeeper, enhancing vendor and contract lifecycle management. Emily's background includes significant contributions as an Executive Board Member at Caim and Strategic Advisor for The Conservation Project International, alongside leadership roles at Ometria, Triptease, EyeforTravel, and moneycorp. Emily holds a degree in English Literature and Publishing from Loughborough University.

# Emily Assender
[...]
### COO & Co-founder
[...]
Emily Assender is a seasoned executive with extensive experience in strategic partnerships and business development across various industries. Currently serving as COO and Co-founder at Revelesco since March 2024, Emily leads efforts to provide critical coaching and strategic support for startups and scaleups. Previously, Emily held roles such as Director at Okra Partners Ltd., focusing on building partnerships for B2B SaaS businesses, and Vice President of Strategic Partnerships at Gatekeeper, enhancing vendor and contract lifecycle management. Emily's background includes significant contributions as an Executive Board Member at Caim and Strategic Advisor for The Conservation Project International, alongside leadership roles at Ometria, Triptease, EyeforTravel, and moneycorp. Emily holds a degree in English Literature and Publishing from Loughborough University.
